meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Temsirolimus is the intravenous rapamycin analogue, and, to our knowledge, the first mTOR inhibitor to show an overall-survival benefit in a randomised trial.
data.mechanism_beginner: Temsirolimus is the IV version of rapamycin and, as far as we know, the first mTOR-blocking drug shown to help patients live longer in a controlled trial (in advanced kidney cancer).
data.boundary: HUD2007 shows the clinical effect (overall survival in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer). It did not measure mTORC1 activity; that temsirolimus inhibits mTORC1 rests on the FKBP12-dependent mechanism it shares with rapamycin.
data.note: 2026-10-10: beginner text hedged to match the expert text ('to our knowledge'); boundary added that the cited trial is clinical, not pharmacodynamic.
